properties.SITE_NAME: GLENBURN MUNICIPAL C AND D LANDFILL
properties.SUMMARY:
THERE ARE 2 LANDFILLS SIDE-BY-SIDE AT THIS LOCATION. THE FIRST IS A PROJECT THAT INVOLVED THE CLOSING OF THE TOWN OF GLENBURN'S MUNICIPAL SOLID WASTE LANDFILL. THE ENTIRE SITE COMPRISED OF 156 ACRES WHILE THE SOLID WASTE BOUNDARY ENCLOSES APPROX. 2.5 ACRES WHICH HAS BEEN UTILIZED FOR OVER 20 YEARS. THIS LANDFILL IS A SANITARY ATTENUATION LANDFILL ACCEPTING ONLY MUNICIPAL SOLID WASTE GENERATED BY RESIDENTS OF TOWN OF GLENBURN. IN 1983, THE TOWN RECEIVED APPROVAL FOR EXPANSION (PHASE II). PHASE II WAS PROPOSED AND DISCUSSED, HOWEVER FINAL APPROVAL FOR CONSTRUCTION WAS NEVER GRANTED. THE TOWN SUBMITTED AN APPLICATION TO RELICENSE PHASE II IN AUGUST 0F 1991 AS A BACKUP DISPOSAL OPTION TO ALLOW CONTINUED USE OF THE METALS, TIRES, WOODWASTE, AND DEMOLITION AREAS. APPROVAL GRANTED ON 9-5-91 FOR CLOSURE PLAN.

THE SECOND LOCATION IS A 2 ACRE LANDFILL CLOSED IN 1991 AS REQUIRED BY THE MEDEP LANDFILL CLOSURE AND REMEDIATION PROGRAM.   THE LANDFILL CLOSURE USED THE REGULATION CLOSURE PROCEDURE.  THIS GENERALLY CONSISTED OF AN ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT, A CLAY OR COMPOSITE COVER SYSTEM, AND WATER QUALITY MONITORING.  SPECIFIC DETAILS FOR CLOSURE OF THIS LANDFILL ARE AVAILABLE THROUGH MEDEP FILE ROOM.

properties.SUMMARY:
THE HARRISON LANDFILL IS CONSIDERED A GRANDFATHERED SITE - ESTABLISHED PRIOR TO 1973. THE TOWN WAS GIVEN A 3 YEAR PERMIT TO USE THIS SITE IN SEPTEMBER, 1981, AND THE SITE WAS TO HAVE BEEN COMPLETELY CLOSED AND CAPPED BY OCTOBER, 1984. THE TOWN RECEIVED APPROVAL ON 4-21-89 FOR CONSTRUCTION OF A NEW TRANSFER STATION SOUTH OF THE LANDFILL SITE. THE TOWN THEN PROPOSED TO CLOSE THE LANDFILL IN 2 PHASES. PHASE 1. STOP AND CLOSE MSW SECTION OF DUMP. PHASE 2. CLOSE THE SHORT TERM WOOD WASTE AND DEMO DEBRIS AREA OF APPROX. 1.5 ACRES THE INTERIM CLOSING PLAN WAS APPROVED ON 8 AUGUST 1991.

properties.SITE_NAME: MID-COAST SOLID WASTE QUARRY LANDFILL AND TRANSFER STATION
properties.DESCRIPTION: 4 ACRE ACTIVE LANDFILL.  THE AREA KNOWN AS JACOBS QUARRY HAS BEEN USED BY THE TOWNS OF CAMDEN, HOPE, LINCOLNVILLE AND ROCKPORT TO DISPOSE OF VARIOUS TYPES OF SOLID WASTE SINCE ABOUT 1930. TANNERY WASTE WAS DISPOSED OF FOR A WHILE. IN 1983 THE FOUR PARTICIPATING TOWNS DISCONTINUED THE PRACTICE OF LANDFILLING MUNICIPAL SOLID WASTE, HOWEVER, THE QUARRY SITE HAS CONTINUED TO RECEIVE TREES AND BRUSH, CONSTRUCTION DEBRIS, AND OTHER WOOD WASTE. IT HAS BEEN THE TOWNS DESIRE TO KEEP THE SITE AVAILABLE FOR THIS USE, ALTHOUGH DEP PRESSURE TO COMPLETELY CLOSEOUT AND PROVIDE REMEDIAL CLEAN-UP AT THE SITE HAS BEEN MOUNTING OVER THE YEARS. IT WAS RECOGNIZED THAT SURFACE RUNOFF WAS BEING CONTAMINATED. NO FURTHER DISPOSAL OF ANYTHING IN THE QUARRY WAS STRONGLY RECOMMENDED.
